SparkR / SPARKR-237
private package functions unavailable when using lapplyPartition in package
Issue Type: Bug
Assignee: Unassigned
Created: 19/Mar/15 1:48 PM
Priority: Major
Reporter: Antonio Piccolboni

Developing package that imports SparkR. There is a function in that package that calls lapplyPartition with a function argument that uses in its body some functions private to the package. When run, the computation fails because R can not find the private function (details below). If I fully qualify them with otherpackage:::private.function, the error moves down to the next private function. This used to work some time ago, I've been working on other stuff for a little while. This should also work by regular R scope rules. I apologize I don't have a minimal test case ready, but this was discovered developing plyrmr and the list of dependencies is long enough that it's a little bit of a burden to make you install it. I think I can put together a toy package to demonstrate the problem, if that helps.

Re: private package functions unavailable when using lapplyPartition in package

I would like to summarize the discussion that went on in a pull request https://github.com/RevolutionAnalytics/plyrmr/pull/72 to unify the subject under this ticket.
What it appears is that this problem depends of replacing getDependencies with cleanClosure and that it is unfixable in the short term. @hao proposed workarounds for dependent packages that include: fully qualifying all function calls; rename some variables according to unstated rules; modifying enclosing environment for promises in a way that is neither backward compatible nor consistent with R semantics (promises are not limited to one enclosing environment equal to GlobalEnv). These are extremely heavy handed, breaking the package in other ways and would be impossible to hide from the end user as the API accepts user defined functions and expressions in several if not most calls. So I am not trying to be difficult, but we can't adopt the workarounds. Considering that SparkR-238 is still open and probably related, my suggestion would be to revert to getDependencies for the moment being and make changes incrementally from there. @hao says getDependencies had correctness issues as well but I would like some detail about it, as plyrmr tests as well SparkR's own passed before cleanClosure was merged.
